meta_description: Zero-trust segmentation for clinical networks — lateral-movement paths cut by 87% and the national security audit passed without conditions

blocks.x: Zero-trust segmentation for clinical networks — lateral-movement paths cut by 87% and the national security audit passed without conditions

Identity withheld — a national health service agency whose clinical estate had grown hospital by hospital, network by network, with flat trust between them all. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.

The baseline assessment mapped the flatness: 1,340 workstations able to reach clinical systems directly, a single compromised laptop in one region able to traverse to pharmacy systems in another, and an audit finding list the agency had carried for two cycles.
The constraint was clinical, not technical: segmentation could not touch care delivery uptime, and the previous attempt had been abandoned after a ward went offline.

We ran segmentation as clinical gates: zones designed around care workflows, pilot wards with clinical sign-off before each wave, fallback paths tested with the wards' own downtime procedures, and the audit findings tracked to evidence the national reviewers walked. The flat network retired zone by zone, with clinicians holding the cutover authority throughout.
